title: Outlook: custom organisation properties on profile cards
summary: Hold: the risk rationale wrongly implies that ingested people data remains unexposed until a property is made visible on profile cards, although Microsoft documents other consumers of that data. The open questions also cast doubt on per-property visibility, which Microsoft's supplied notice explicitly documents.

claims.quote: These properties can be sourced from external systems like HR platforms, enriching user profiles with relevant organizational details.

claims.fix: Replace the first open question with 'Is there a tenant-wide switch for the whole feature, in addition to the per-property visibility documented in MC1193692?' The supplied notice explicitly confirms per-property visibility.

claims.where: rationale: risk; Governance guidance: Leave properties hidden
claims.claim: Nothing is exposed until an administrator both ingests data and makes a property visible on profile cards.
claims.quote: By default, people data provided via a Copilot connector is visible to all users in the tenant.
claims.fix: Change the rationale to 'Low. The new card-display feature requires admin configuration. Ingested people data can already be visible through other Microsoft 365 experiences, so approve data before ingestion, not merely before card visibility is enabled.' Change rollout guidance to require HR validation before ingestion; hiding card properties is not a data-access boundary.

claims.claim: Every control the governance checklist asks administrators to configure or check is represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Choose or build the people-data connector' and 'Check your connector item quota'; table: only custom-property visibility and existing Entra profile-card properties.
claims.fix: Add a people-data connection setup row using the documented Connectors gallery and Microsoft Graph external connections APIs, with the role discrepancy noted. Add an item-quota row only after reading its management surface, or remove the quota-check instruction from the checklist and retain it as an unresolved licensing question.

claims.claim: Learn does not yet describe the new connector-custom-property display-name, icon and visibility configuration; the cited profile-card article covers related existing settings.
